mainTopic: The doubled holy מנה; רבי חנינא's questions to רבי אליעזר; an animal born unlike its mother and בכורה, and the sources of the תנא of our משנה and רבי יוסי הגלילי
overview: This amud opens by finishing a calculation from a verse in יחזקאל. From it the גמרא learns three things: the מנה של קודש was double size, a community may enlarge its measures by up to a sixth, and that sixth is counted 'from outside', meaning a sixth of the final total. Next, רבי חנינא reports questions he asked רבי אליעזר. First he asked why only firstborn donkeys are redeemed, and was told it is a גזירת הכתוב and that donkeys carried Egypt's wealth at יציאת מצרים. He then asked about the names רפידים and שטים. רבי אליעזר says they are just names, while רבי יהושע reads them as hints at ישראל's failings, and the two also argue over the verse 'ותקראן לעם'. A new משנה then rules that an animal born unlike its mother is exempt from בכורה, learned from 'פטר חמור' written twice. It adds that for eating, the mother alone decides: what comes from טמא is טמא, and what comes from טהור is טהור. The גמרא shows that רב יהודה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who learns the same-species rule from 'בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז'. It explains that the two views differ on whether the Torah wrote the rule about קדושת דמים or about קדושת הגוף, and it works through a צריכותא showing that all three animals are needed for burning the אימורין. Finally, the גמרא explains that רבי יוסי הגלילי uses 'פטר חמור' to exclude horses and camels from redemption, and the amud ends with a challenge to that reading that is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: The numbers don't add up to a מנה
steps.stepSummary: The verse's sixty shekels equal 240 dinars, far more than a standard מנה of 100 dinars.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that comes out to two hundred and forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a math problem in the verse from יחזקאל it was just discussing. The verse's total does not match the normal value of a מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse adds 20 + 25 + 15 shekels and calls the total a מנה, so a מנה would be 60 shekels. Each shekel is 4 dinars, so 60 shekels equal 240 dinars. A normal מנה is only 100 dinars, so the verse seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of money or weight, normally 100 dinars

steps.confusionAlert: The 240 is counted in dinars, not shekels. Sixty shekels times four dinars each equals 240 dinars.

phrases.english: But they come to two hundred and forty!
phrases.notes: Sixty shekels at four dinars each is 240 dinars, but a regular מנה is only 100.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the calculation from the verse in יחזקאל quoted on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The verse's statement that 60 shekels make up a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 60 shekels = 240 dinars, but a מנה = 100 dinars. The verse's total is far too big.

steps.title: The holy מנה was double size
steps.stepSummary: The resolution is that the מנה של קודש was worth double: 200 dinars, which is 50 shekels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the holy מנה was a doubled מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the math problem by saying that the מנה used for holy matters was twice the size of a regular one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubled מנה is 200 dinars, which equals 50 shekels. That closes most of the gap, but the verse still says 60 shekels, not 50. The extra 10 shekels will be explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather', rejecting the problem and offering a new understanding
'Learn from it', a conclusion drawn from the source
The מנה used for holy/Temple purposes

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ מָנֶה כָּפוּל הָיָה.
phrases.english: the maneh of the Sanctuary was a doubled maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the math problem raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the unit: the holy מנה is a different, larger measure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That the verse means a regular 100-dinar מנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The holy מנה is double, 200 dinars (50 shekels)

steps.title: Measures may be increased up to one sixth, counted from outside
steps.stepSummary: The leftover 10 shekels teach that measures may be enlarged, by no more than a sixth, and that the sixth is counted from the final total.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it that we may add to measures, but not more than a sixth. And learn from it that the sixth is counted from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the extra 10 shekels, 60 instead of 50. From this it draws two more practical rules about changing measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל's מנה is 60, which is 10 more than the 50-shekel doubled מנה. So it is allowed to enlarge measures. Those 10 shekels are one sixth of the final 60, but one fifth of the original 50. This shows the maximum increase is a sixth 'from outside', meaning a sixth of the new total.

keyTerms.meaning: We may add to (enlarge) the standard measures
'From outside': counted from the final total

steps.whatToRemember: From the verse in יחזקאל: (1) the מנה של קודש was double; (2) measures may be enlarged by up to a שתות; (3) the שתות is מלבר, a sixth of the new total, which equals a fifth of the old amount.
steps.confusionAlert: 'A sixth from outside' does not mean adding a sixth of the original amount. It means the added part is a sixth of the final sum, which is actually a fifth of the original.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic limit on how much a community may change official measures.

phrases.english: And learn from it: we may increase measures,
but we may not increase by more than a sixth,
and learn from it that the sixth is from the outside.
phrases.notes: 10 is a sixth of 60 (the final total) and a fifth of 50.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the leftover 10 shekels that step 2 did not cover.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Measures may be increased by up to a sixth of the final total (a fifth of the original).

steps.title: Why only donkeys among non-kosher firstborns?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא asks רבי אליעזר why firstborn donkeys are redeemed, but not firstborn horses or camels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: I asked רבי אליעזר in the great study hall: Why are firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of פטר חמור. It quotes a question רבי חנינא once asked his teacher about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horses, camels and donkeys are all non-kosher animals. Yet only a firstborn donkey needs פדיון, being redeemed with a lamb. The question asks what makes donkeys special.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
I asked Rabbi Eliezer
in the great study hall,
how are firstborn donkeys different
from firstborn horses and camels?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נִשְׁתַּנּוּ פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים מִפִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns from the measures discussion to פטר חמור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason donkeys alone among non-kosher animals have firstborn sanctity

steps.title: A Torah decree, and the donkeys helped at the Exodus
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that it is a גזירת הכתוב. He adds that donkeys helped the Jews leave מצרים carrying Egyptian wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: It is a decree of the Torah. And also, the donkeys helped the Jewish people when they left מצרים. Every single Jew had ninety Nubian donkeys loaded with Egypt's silver and gold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives two answers. The main one is that the Torah simply commanded it. The second offers a meaningful reason: donkeys served the Jews at יציאת מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer, גזירת הכתוב, means no logical reason is needed. The rule stands because the verse says so. The second answer ('ועוד') adds a fitting explanation: donkeys earned this special status by helping the Jews, carrying Egypt's silver and gold out of מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree of the verse: a Torah law given without a stated reason

steps.whatToRemember: פטר חמור is mainly a גזירת הכתוב. The added reason is that donkeys carried Egypt's wealth at יציאת מצרים.

phrases.english: He said to me: It is a decree of the verse,
and furthermore, because they assisted Israel
at the time of their exodus from Egypt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָךְ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: for there was not a single one of Israel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עִמּוֹ תִּשְׁעִים חֲמוֹרִים לוּבִים
phrases.english: who did not have with him ninety Nubian donkeys
laden with the silver and gold of Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חנינא's question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a גזירת הכתוב. Also, donkeys helped the Jews at the Exodus by carrying Egyptian wealth.

steps.title: What does the name רפידים mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא asked רבי אליעזר a second question: the meaning of the place-name רפידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also asked him: What is the meaning of the word 'רפידים'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא continues his report with a second, unrelated question. He asks about רפידים, where עמלק attacked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks whether רפידים is just a geographic name or whether it hints at something. This sets up a disagreement about whether the name carries a message.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where עמלק attacked Israel (שמות יז:ח)
'What is the meaning of the expression?'

phrases.english: And furthermore I asked him:
What is the meaning of the term “Rephidim”?
phrases.notes: This is the place where עמלק attacked (שמות יז:ח).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question in the same report by רבי חנינא, on a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the name רפידים has a hidden meaning

steps.title: רפידים is simply its name
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that רפידים is just the name of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: רפידים was its name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers that the name has no special hidden message. It is simply what the place was called.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'רפידים שמה', רבי אליעזר rejects reading a lesson into the name. The גמרא will next show that this is one side of a תנאים dispute.

phrases.english: And he said to me: Rephidim is its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רפידים is simply the place's name.

steps.title: This matches a dispute of תנאים: רבי אליעזר's side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this answer follows one side of a תנאים dispute, where רבי אליעזר says רפידים is just the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: רבי אליעזר says רפידים was its name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the answer to a known תנאים dispute and presents the first side. This sets up the opposing view that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כתנאי' tells us the question was argued by תנאים. רבי אליעזר's view in the ברייתא is the same as the answer he gave רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like a dispute of תנאים': this matches an earlier argument

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between tanna'im:
Rabbi Eliezer says: Rephidim is its name,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places step 7's answer within a תנאים dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: רפידים is simply the place's name.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: they grew lax in Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reads רפידים as a hint that Israel became weak (ריפו) in Torah, and supports the meaning with a verse about 'רפיון ידים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: It was called that because they became lax in the words of Torah. And so the verse says: 'Fathers did not turn back to their children because of weakness of hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The other side of the dispute: רבי יהושע says the name is a hint. It is related to the root רפה, meaning weak or slack, and teaches that the people slackened in Torah study there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע links רפידים to 'ריפו', 'they weakened'. He brings a verse from ירמיהו showing that the root means weakness (רפיון ידים). The גמרא here only explains the name רפידים; it does not mention עמלק.

keyTerms.meaning: That they made themselves lax / slackened
'And so it says', introducing a supporting verse

steps.whatToRemember: Dispute: רבי אליעזר says רפידים is just a name. רבי יהושע says it hints that Israel 'ריפו', grew lax in Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the idea that weakness in Torah opens the door to עמלק's attack.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
that they became lax with regard to the words of Torah,
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: רפידים sounds like ריפו, 'they went slack.'

phrases.english: and so it says:
“The fathers do not turn back to their children
because of feebleness of hands.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁרִיפּוּ עַצְמָן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing side of the תנאים dispute begun in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: the name רפידים alludes to Israel growing lax in Torah, supported by 'רפיון ידים'.

steps.title: Another question: what does the name שטים mean
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports that he also asked רבי אליעזר about the meaning of the place-name שטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also asked him: what is the meaning of the word 'שטים'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is another question in the same list that רבי חנינא asked רבי אליעזר. This time he asks about the name שטים, the place where בני ישראל camped before the sin with the daughters of מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has the same shape as the earlier question about רפידים. רבי חנינא wants to know whether the name hints at something that happened there.

keyTerms.meaning: שטים, the place where ישראל camped (במדבר כה:א)

phrases.english: And furthermore I asked him:
What is the meaning of the term 'Shittim'?
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'וישב ישראל בשטים' (במדבר כה:א).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the list, built just like the רפידים question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the name שטים carry a hidden meaning?

steps.title: Answer: שטים is simply the name
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that שטים is just the name of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: שטים is its name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the same kind of answer he gave for רפידים. The name is only a name and does not hint at anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is consistent with how רבי אליעזר treated רפידים. He does not read the place-names in this section as hints.

phrases.english: And he said to me: Shittim is its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שטים is a plain place-name with no hidden meaning.

steps.title: This follows one side of a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this answer matches רבי אליעזר's view in a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: רבי אליעזר says, שטים is its name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in to say that the answer is not unique. It matches one side of a known dispute. This line also sets up the opposing view that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as with רפידים in step 8. רבי אליעזר's plain reading here is one opinion in a בריתא.

phrases.english: Like a dispute between tanna'im:
Rabbi Eliezer says: Shittim is its name,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the answer of step 11 inside a dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: שטים is just the place's name.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: שטים hints at foolishness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reads שטים as a hint that the people busied themselves with שטות, meaning foolish and sinful behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: it is called this because they busied themselves with matters of foolishness.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the dispute. רבי יהושע says the name hints at what the people did there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע connects the sound of שטים to שטות. This refers to the זנות and עבודה זרה described in במדבר כה. It matches his approach with רפידים, where he also read the name as a hint about ישראל's failing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
That they were engaged in matters of nonsense.
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: שטים sounds like שטות, 'nonsense.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי אליעזר's view in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: שטים hints at the people's involvement in שטות.

steps.title: Second dispute on 'they called the people': רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: On the verse 'ותקראן לעם', רבי אליעזר explains that undressed women met them.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the verse 'And they called the people to the offerings of their gods', רבי אליעזר says: naked women met them.
steps.whatsHappening: The same two תנאים argue about another verse from the same story. Here רבי אליעזר explains how the people were drawn into the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads the word ותקראן as related to 'meeting' (לקראת). The daughters of מואב came out to meet the men without proper clothing. That is how the men were drawn to their idols.

phrases.english: 'And they called the people to the offerings of their gods' —
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Naked women encountered them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second dispute between the same תנאים on the next verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: ותקראן means the women came out to meet them, undressed.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: they all became impure through emission
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reads ותקראן as related to קרי. The men all became בעלי קרי because of their lust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: they all became people who had experienced seminal emissions.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי יהושע's side of the second dispute. He reads the same word in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע hears ותקראן as connected to the word קרי. The lust that the women stirred up caused the men to become בעלי קרי. This ends the אגדה section of the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: People who experienced a seminal emission

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
That they all became those who experienced seminal emissions.
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: ותקראן sounds like קרי, a seminal emission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to step 14. It closes the אגדה section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: ותקראן hints that they all became בעלי קרי.

steps.title: משנה: an animal born unlike its mother is exempt from firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a cow that gave birth to something like a donkey, or a donkey that gave birth to something like a horse, is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A cow that gave birth to a kind of donkey, and a donkey that gave birth to a kind of horse, are exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here and the topic changes back to הלכה. It rules that a mixed-looking birth, where the baby looks like a different species from the mother, is not a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are given. In the first, a kosher mother has a baby that looks like a donkey. In the second, a donkey has a baby that looks like a horse. In both cases, the baby does not get the holiness of a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the opening of a new משנה)
Exempt from the laws of the firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: 'כמין חמור' means the baby only LOOKS like a donkey. It does not mean a true donkey was born from a cow.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts,
And a donkey that gave birth to a horse of sorts —
Are exempt from the firstborn status,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It changes the topic from אגדה back to the laws of בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A birth unlike its mother's species is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: Source: 'firstborn of a donkey' is written twice
steps.stepSummary: The משנה proves its rule from the fact that the Torah writes פטר חמור twice. This teaches that both the mother and the baby must be donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says 'firstborn of a donkey', 'firstborn of a donkey', two times. This teaches that the law applies only when the one giving birth is a donkey and the one born is a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the Torah source for its ruling. The repetition in the verses is the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One mention of פטר חמור teaches that the mother must be a donkey. The second mention teaches that the baby must also be a donkey. If either one is missing, there is no obligation of פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn of a donkey (redeemed with a lamb)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that בכורה requires both mother and baby to be the same species. The גמרא will build on this rule.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'firstborn of a donkey', 'firstborn of a donkey'
Twice,
Not unless the birth mother is a donkey
And the one born is a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the ruling in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The exemption of a birth unlike its mother from בכורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The double mention of פטר חמור in the Torah.

steps.title: משנה asks: can these animals be eaten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what the law is for eating such an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is their status regarding eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a second question about the same strange births. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the issue was בכורה. Now the משנה asks whether the kashrus of such a baby follows its mother or its own appearance.

phrases.english: And what are they with regard to consumption?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the בכורה question to the eating question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the kashrus of an unusual birth follow the mother or the baby's appearance?

steps.title: Kashrus follows the mother
steps.stepSummary: A baby born from a kosher animal is permitted even if it looks non-kosher. A baby born from a non-kosher animal is forbidden even if it looks kosher. What comes from the טמא is טמא, and what comes from the טהור is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kosher animal that gave birth to something like a non-kosher animal: it is permitted to eat. A non-kosher animal that gave birth to something like a kosher animal: it is forbidden to eat. This is because what comes out of the non-kosher is non-kosher, and what comes out of the kosher is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers that only the mother decides whether the baby may be eaten. Then it states the general rule behind this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby's appearance does not matter at all. The source of the baby decides its status. The משנה sums this up in a short rule: היוצא מן הטמא טמא, היוצא מן הטהור טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever comes from a non-kosher source is non-kosher

steps.whatToRemember: For בכורה, both the mother and the baby must be the same species (פטר חמור is written twice). For eating, the mother alone decides. What comes from טמא is טמא, and what comes from טהור is טהור.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not judge by looks. A baby that looks like a non-kosher animal but was born to a kosher mother may be eaten.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה —
phrases.english: A kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher animal of sorts —
Is permitted for consumption,
And a non-kosher animal that gave birth to a kosher animal of sorts —
Is prohibited for consumption,
Because that which emerges from the non-kosher is non-kosher,
And that which emerges from the kosher is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the eating question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kashrus follows the mother. What comes from טמא is טמא, and what comes from טהור is טהור.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes a related משנה about a ewe and a goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by quoting a משנה from elsewhere. A ewe that gave birth to a goat-type, or a goat that gave birth to a ewe-type, is exempt from בכורה. If the baby has some of its mother's signs, it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה there: A ewe that gave birth to a goat-type, and a goat that gave birth to a ewe-type, are exempt from the firstborn law. If the baby has some of its mother's signs, it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a similar משנה from later in the מסכת, about two kosher animals giving birth to each other's type. It is setting up a question about the source of that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה dealt with a cow giving birth to a donkey-type baby. This new משנה is about a ewe and a goat, which are both kosher animals. It also adds a new detail: a baby that has only some of the mother's signs is obligated in בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Some of the identifying signs (of the mother's species)
The status and law of a firstborn animal

steps.confusionAlert: Both a sheep and a goat are kosher animals. The exemption here is not about kosher versus non-kosher. It is about the baby being a different species from its mother.

phrases.english: Gemara:
We learned there (in another mishna):
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה on 16b.

phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a goat-type,
and a goat that gave birth to a ewe-type —
is exempt from the firstborn obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and if it has some of the (mother's) signs — it is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel משנה, about kosher species born from each other, alongside our משנה's cow and donkey case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ewe or goat giving birth to the other's type is exempt from בכורה. If the baby has some of the mother's signs, it is obligated.

steps.title: Asking for the source of this rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this law comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the ewe and goat rule. It is setting up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not challenging the rule. It wants to know which verse teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: From where are these matters (derived)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches that a ewe or goat born from the other species is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the mother and baby must be the same species
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה derives the rule from the verse 'the firstborn of an ox, the firstborn of a lamb, the firstborn of a goat.' Both the mother and the firstborn must be the same species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The verse says 'But the firstborn of an ox.' This means the mother must be an ox and its firstborn an ox. 'The firstborn of a lamb' means the mother must be a lamb and its firstborn a lamb. 'The firstborn of a goat' means the mother must be a goat and its firstborn a goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question with a verse from במדבר (18:17). He reads each phrase as requiring the mother and the baby to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have simply listed 'ox, lamb, goat.' Saying 'firstborn of an ox' shows that both the parent and the firstborn must be oxen. So a ewe's goat-type baby is not 'a firstborn of a lamb,' and it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The mother must be an ox and its firstborn an ox

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic principle: the law of בכורה applies only when the baby's species matches its mother's.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said,
for the verse says: 'But the firstborn of an ox' —
that it (the mother) must be an ox and its firstborn an ox,

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב״ — שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא כֶּשֶׂב וּבְכוֹרוֹ כֶּשֶׂב,
phrases.english: 'the firstborn of a lamb' — that it must be a lamb and its firstborn a lamb,
'the firstborn of a goat' —
that it must be a goat and its firstborn a goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrases 'בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז' (במדבר 18:17) teach that the mother and the firstborn must be the same species.

steps.title: The word 'but' teaches that partial signs still count
steps.stepSummary: One might think a baby with only some of the mother's signs is also exempt. The word אך limits the exemption, so such a baby is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the baby is exempt even if it has some of the mother's signs. Therefore the verse says 'But,' which makes a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The derivation continues with the second half of the משנה. It shows the source for 'if it has some signs, it is obligated.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might assume that any baby that is not fully like its mother is exempt. The word אך is read as a limiting word. It separates out the partial-signs case and keeps it obligated in בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (introduces a wrong assumption)
'But / only': a limiting word in the verse

steps.confusionAlert: The word אך does not cancel the exemption. It only carves out the case of a baby with some of the mother's signs.
steps.whatToRemember: A full different-species baby is exempt from בכורה (from 'בכור שור'). A baby with some of the mother's signs is obligated (from 'אך').

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין?
phrases.english: One might think (it is exempt) even if it has some of the signs?
The verse teaches: 'But' — it made a distinction.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב יהודה's derivation to cover the 'some signs' clause.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a baby with some of the mother's signs is obligated in בכורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting word 'אך' in 'אך בכור שור' (במדבר 18:17).

steps.title: Challenge: our משנה already used the doubled word פטר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. Our משנה's תנא learned the cow and donkey case from the doubled word 'פטר'. Why does רב יהודה need a different verse?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא of our משנה takes 'פטר... פטר' as the source for the case of a cow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יהודה. Our own משנה already had a source for this kind of rule: 'פטר חמור' is written twice. So why look for a new verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, our משנה learned from 'פטר חמור' written twice that the mother and baby must both be donkeys. That covered a cow giving birth to a donkey-type. If the doubled פטר teaches 'same species' there, it seems it should work for the ewe and goat case too. That would make רב יהודה's verse unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Firstborn' (literally, 'the one that opens the womb'); the word appears twice in the verses about פטר חמור

phrases.english: But the tanna (takes) 'firstborn' 'firstborn'
as his source, for (the case of) a cow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's derivation by pointing to the source our משנה already used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's use of 'בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז' as the source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה already learns the 'same species' requirement from the doubled 'פטר' for a cow. So רב יהודה's separate derivation seems redundant, or seems to conflict with the תנא's method.

steps.title: רב יהודה follows a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's derivation comes from רבי יוסי הגלילי, who reads 'ox, lamb, goat' as requiring the mother and the baby to be the same species.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says it in line with רבי יוסי הגלילי. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the verse 'But the firstborn of an ox' means it must be an ox and its firstborn an ox. 'The firstborn of a lamb' means it must be a lamb and its firstborn a lamb. 'Or the firstborn of a goat' means it must be a goat and its firstborn a goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. רב יהודה is not making up a new derivation. He is following an earlier תנא, רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was: why does רב יהודה need the ox, lamb and goat verse if our משנה already uses the doubled word פטר? The answer is that this is a real disagreement between תנאים. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads each animal in the verse as requiring the mother and the baby to be the same kind.

keyTerms.meaning: He said it in accordance with (someone): his statement follows an earlier authority
Unless it is / only when it is

steps.confusionAlert: 'הוא שור ובכורו שור' means the mother is an ox and her baby is an ox. 'הוא' refers to the mother, not to the baby.

phrases.english: He says it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
as it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"But the firstborn of an ox" —

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר,
phrases.english: only when it (the mother) is an ox and its firstborn is an ox;
"the firstborn of a lamb" —

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא כֶּשֶׂב וּבְכוֹרוֹ כֶּשֶׂב,
phrases.english: only when it is a lamb and its firstborn is a lamb;
"or the firstborn of a goat" —

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא עֵז וּבְכוֹרוֹ עֵז.
phrases.english: only when it is a goat and its firstborn is a goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by tracing רב יהודה's source to a תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה seemed to need a new verse for no reason, since our משנה already had a source.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who uses the ox, lamb and goat verse instead of פטר-פטר.

steps.title: The word אך keeps a partly-similar baby obligated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one might think a baby with only some of its mother's signs is exempt, so the word אך makes a distinction and keeps it obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the exemption applies even if the baby has some of its mother's signs. So the verse says 'אך' to make a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי continues. It gives the exact source for the second half of רב יהודה's teaching, the limit made by אך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the reading of אך in step 23 also comes from רבי יוסי הגלילי. The word אך divides the cases: a totally different-looking baby is exempt, but a baby with some of its mother's signs is still a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (to rule this out)
Some of the identifying signs (of the mother)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין?
phrases.english: One might think that even if it has some of the signs (it is exempt)?
The verse teaches: "But" — it made a distinction.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 25, matching רב יהודה's use of אך in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading that אך keeps a partly-similar baby obligated
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: What is the real disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle makes our משנה's תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי use different verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the two תנאים learn the same law from different verses. This sets up the explanation in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree on the final law: a baby that looks like a different species is exempt. The question is why they picked different sources. The גמרא wants the underlying idea that splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Opening of the womb': the word used for the firstborn, doubled in the donkey verses

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having found two sources for one law, the גמרא asks what the root of the difference is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that leads our משנה's תנא and רבי יוסי הגלילי to different verses

steps.title: Our משנה: the rule was written for the donkey
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה's תנא holds that the Torah wrote the rule about the donkey, which has קדושת דמים, and the same applies to kosher animals, which have קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of our משנה holds: the Torah revealed the rule in the case of קדושת דמים, and the same is true for קדושת הגוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with the view of our משנה's תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The firstborn donkey is not itself holy. It is redeemed with a lamb, so only its value is holy (קדושת דמים). Our תנא learns 'must look like its mother' from the doubled פטר written about the donkey. He then applies it to kosher firstborn animals, which are themselves holy and go on the מזבח (קדושת הגוף).

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness of value: the item is redeemed rather than offered (here, the firstborn donkey)
Holiness of the body itself: the animal is offered on the מזבח (here, a kosher firstborn)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of holiness. In this סוגיא, קדושת דמים means the donkey and קדושת הגוף means the kosher animals (ox, lamb, goat).

phrases.english: The tanna of our mishna holds:
the Merciful One revealed it regarding sanctity of value (the donkey),
and the same is true regarding inherent sanctity (kosher animals).

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא דִידַן סָבַר: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּקְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer to step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our תנא learns from the donkey verse (קדושת דמים) and extends the rule to קדושת הגוף.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the rule was written for kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that the Torah wrote the rule about kosher animals (קדושת הגוף), and the donkey (קדושת דמים) is learned from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי holds: the Torah revealed the rule in the case of קדושת הגוף, and the same is true for קדושת דמים. He learns קדושת דמים from קדושת הגוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer with רבי יוסי הגלילי's view, which runs the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the main source is the ox, lamb and goat verse, which is about kosher animals with קדושת הגוף. He then derives the donkey law from it. So both תנאים agree on the law. They only disagree about which case the Torah wrote it for and which case is learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives / learns (one case from another)
The firstborn donkey, redeemed with a lamb
From the case of inherent sanctity

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a firstborn must look like its mother's species, and that a baby with some of her signs is still a בכור. The only question is direction. Our משנה's תנא learns kosher animals from the donkey (פטר-פטר). רבי יוסי הגלילי, followed by רב יהודה, learns the donkey from kosher animals (ox, lamb, goat).
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רב יהודה needed his own verse: he follows a different תנא, who treats the kosher-animal verse as the primary source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
the Merciful One revealed it regarding inherent sanctity (kosher animals),
and the same is true regarding sanctity of value (the donkey),
and he derives sanctity of value from inherent sanctity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by giving the opposite view to step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי learns from the kosher-animal verse (קדושת הגוף) and derives the donkey (קדושת דמים) from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two תנאים differ only on which kind of holiness the Torah wrote the rule about. That is why רב יהודה, following רבי יוסי הגלילי, uses a different verse.

steps.title: What does our תנא do with the repeated word בכור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what our משנה's תנא learns from the repeated word 'בכור', since he does not use it the way רבי יוסי הגלילי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא: what does he do with this 'firstborn', 'firstborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. Our תנא gets the same-species rule from a different verse, so what does he learn from the extra word 'בכור'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule: every extra word in the Torah must teach something. רבי יוסי הגלילי used the repeated 'בכור' to require that mother and baby be the same species. Our תנא does not use it that way, so he needs some other use for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
What does he do with it? This asks what a scholar learns from a verse he did not use for the rule under discussion
Firstborn. The word is repeated in the verse for ox, lamb, and goat

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on our תנא. It is a standard question: if he does not use this verse for this rule, what does he use it for?

phrases.english: And the tanna of our mishna,
this 'firstborn', 'firstborn' (repetition)
phrases.notes: The פסוק says בכור שור, בכור כשב, בכור עז (במדבר יח:יז).

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דִידַן, הַאי ״בְּכוֹר״ ״בְּכוֹר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why the two views use different verses, the גמרא asks how our תנא uses רבי יוסי הגלילי's verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What our תנא learns from the repeated 'בכור' in the verse

steps.title: He needs it for רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא needs the repeated 'בכור' for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our תנא uses the repetition for a different purpose: the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. This sets up the next step, where that teaching is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is already 'used up' by another teaching. That is why our תנא cannot use it for the same-species rule. That teaching is about burning the אימורין of each kind of בכור.

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: He needs it for that of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repetition is used for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching about the אימורין

steps.title: Why are the sacrificial portions mentioned for each type of firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks why the burning of the אימורין is stated separately for a firstborn ox, lamb, and goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Why are אימורין stated for a firstborn ox, אימורין for a firstborn lamb, and אימורין for a firstborn goat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who asks a question. Why did the Torah need to teach the burning of the אימורין for each of the three animals separately? Couldn't one be learned from another?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'ואת חלבם תקטיר', burn their fats. Because 'בכור' is repeated for each animal, it is as if the burning were stated for each one separately. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's question sets up a צריכא: proof that each mention is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The sacrificial portions (fats and certain organs) that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Why were sacrificial portions stated regarding a firstborn ox,
sacrificial portions regarding a firstborn lamb,
and sacrificial portions regarding a firstborn goat?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching mentioned in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the burning of the אימורין had to be stated separately for each of the three animals

steps.title: An ox alone would not teach it, because the ox has more libations
steps.stepSummary: Each mention is needed. If only the ox were written, we might say the ox is special because it gets more נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If the Torah had written it only about a firstborn ox, we would say that is because the ox gets more libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer with a צריכא, showing that each animal needed its own mention. First it explains why the ox alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox offering comes with larger wine נסכים than a lamb or goat. So we might think the ox is more important, and only its אימורין are burned. That is why the Torah could not write the rule only about the ox.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. This introduces a proof that each case had to be written
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Wine libations brought with a קרבן
It has more, or it is given more

phrases.aramaic: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא בִּבְכוֹר שׁוֹר —
phrases.english: It is necessary, for if the Merciful One had written it regarding a firstborn ox,
I would say that is because it has more libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ox alone is not enough, because it has more נסכים

steps.title: A lamb alone would not teach it, because the lamb has its tail
steps.stepSummary: If only the lamb were written, we might say the lamb is special, because its אליה (fat tail) is also burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lamb: we would say that is because it has more, through its fat tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The צריכא continues with the lamb. Its special feature is its fat tail. The next step gives the goat's special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep's fat tail (אליה) is added to its אימורין, so a lamb gives more to the מזבח than an ox or goat. So we might think only the lamb's portions are burned. Each animal has its own special feature, so none can be learned from another.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat tail of a sheep, which is burned on the מזבח along with the אימורין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ox is 'better' overall because of its נסכים. Each animal has its own advantage: the ox has its נסכים, the lamb has its אליה. That is exactly why each one had to be written.

phrases.english: A lamb: because it has more, with its fat tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא from the ox to the lamb.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lamb alone is not enough, because it has the extra אליה

steps.title: The goat is special because of an individual's idol-worship offering
steps.stepSummary: If only the goat (עז) were written, we could say it is special, because a יחיד who sins with עבודה זרה must bring a goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only the goat were written, we might say the goat is special, because it gets an added role with an individual who sinned with idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of reasons why each animal needs its own mention. Now it gives the goat's special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual who sins by mistake with עבודה זרה must bring a female goat as a חטאת. For other mistaken sins he may bring a lamb or a goat. This gives the goat a special role, so we could not learn the ox or lamb from the goat alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Was given an added role or extra use

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three animals has its own special feature: the ox gets more נסכים, the lamb's אליה is burned, and the goat is used for an individual's עבודה זרה offering. So none can be learned from just one other.

phrases.english: [If written only] with a goat — [we would say it is special] since it has an added role
with regard to idol worship by an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֵז — שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last part of the answer begun in steps 33-34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The goat is unique because an individual's mistaken idol-worship sin requires a goat.

steps.title: Why not learn one animal from the other two?
steps.stepSummary: Fine, one animal cannot be learned from one other. But why can't we learn the third animal from the other two together?
steps.simpleTranslation: One cannot be learned from one. But let one be learned from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. It agrees one animal can't teach another, but suggests two animals together could teach the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal has its own special feature, so learning from just one fails. But if two animals both have the law, the law does not depend on either one's special feature, so the third should follow. That would make one of the three verses extra.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the earlier answer was wrong. It accepts that one-from-one fails, and asks only about learning from two together.

phrases.english: One cannot be learned from one,
let one be learned from two!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that all three verses are needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ox, lamb, and goat each need their own verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two animals together cancel out each other's special features, so the third could be learned from them. That makes one verse extra.

steps.title: The ox cannot be learned from the lamb and goat
steps.stepSummary: Which animal could the תורה leave out? Not the ox, because the lamb and goat share a feature the ox lacks: they can be used for a קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one should the Torah not write? Suppose the Merciful One did not write the ox, and we learned it from these others. We could say: what is special about these is that they have an added role with the Paschal offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by testing each animal, to see if it could be left out. This step tests leaving out the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lamb and goat can both be brought as a קרבן פסח, but an ox cannot. So the two together share a special feature the ox does not have, and we could not learn the ox from them.

keyTerms.meaning: What about these? (they are special because...)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the method for answering a 'learn one from two' challenge: find a feature the two share that the third lacks.

phrases.english: With which one should [the Torah] not write [it]?
Suppose the Merciful One did not write it with the ox,
and it would be learned from these [lamb and goat] —
what about these?
They are special since they have an added role with Paschal offerings!
phrases.notes: A קרבן פסח may be a lamb or a goat, never an ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵי לָא לִיכְתּוֹב? לָא לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּשׁוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shared-feature refutation (פירכא) against learning from two
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leave out the ox and learn it from the lamb and goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not possible: lamb and goat are both valid for פסח, which the ox is not.

steps.title: The lamb cannot be learned from the ox and goat
steps.stepSummary: Nor can the lamb be left out, because the ox and goat share a feature the lamb lacks: they are brought by the community (ציבור) for a group sin of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose He did not write the lamb, and we learned it from these others. We could say: what is special about these is that they have an added role with the community's idol worship!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps answering the challenge. It now tests leaving out the lamb, and shows that fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the whole community sins by mistake with עבודה זרה, it brings an ox as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת, but no lamb. So the ox and goat share a special feature the lamb lacks, and the lamb cannot be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: They were given an added role

phrases.english: Suppose He did not write it with the lamb,
and it would be learned from these [ox and goat] —
what about these?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ אֵצֶל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּצִיבּוּר!
phrases.english: They are special since they have an added role with the community's idol worship!
phrases.notes: For a community's idol-worship sin: an ox as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת (במדבר טו:כד).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second part of the answer to step 36, same method as step 37
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shared-feature refutation (פירכא) against learning from two
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leave out the lamb and learn it from the ox and goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not possible: ox and goat are both brought for the community's עבודה זרה, which the lamb is not.

steps.title: The goat cannot be left out either
steps.stepSummary: The goat cannot be learned from the ox and lamb, because the ox and lamb each give the altar something extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose the תורה did not write the goat, and we learned it from the other two. That would not work. The ox and lamb are special because each gives the מזבח something extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes checking the last option. It shows that the goat also cannot be learned from the ox and lamb together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox gets more נסכים (wine and flour offerings) than a goat. The lamb's אליה (fat tail) is burned on the altar, but a goat's is not. So the ox and lamb share a 'giving the altar more' feature the goat lacks, and the learning breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: a feature of 'more', meaning something extra
and let it be learned from these (the other two)

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it regarding a goat,
and let it be learned from these (ox and lamb) —
What is special about these?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶן צַד רִבּוּי אֵצֶל מִזְבֵּחַ!
phrases.english: They have a feature of 'more' at the altar!
phrases.notes: The ox gets more נסכים, and the lamb's אליה is burned on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the third and final part of the answer begun in steps 37 and 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposal to learn the third animal from the other two
steps.terutzResolutionType: מה לצד השוה pushback: the two sources share a feature the third animal lacks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the goat could be learned from the ox and lamb together.
steps.terutzMaskana: No. The ox and lamb share an extra role at the altar that the goat does not have.

steps.title: So all three animals are needed
steps.stepSummary: Since no animal can be learned from the others, the תורה had to write all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, all three are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the whole discussion. Each of the three animals had to be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every possible shortcut failed. One animal can't come from one other (steps 33-35), and none can come from the other two (steps 37-39). So the verse's listing of שור, כשב, and עז is not extra.
steps.whatToRemember: For burning the parts of a בכור on the altar, the תורה had to name the ox, the lamb, and the goat. Each one has a unique feature, so none could be learned from the others.

phrases.english: Therefore, they are (all) necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the צריכותא (necessity) argument.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three animals in the verse are needed for the law of burning the parts on the altar.

steps.title: So how does רבי יוסי הגלילי use this verse?
steps.stepSummary: If the verse is fully used for the altar law, how can רבי יוסי הגלילי also learn from it that a בכור must resemble its mother?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי? (How can he learn his rule from this verse?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge in just two words. It is setting up the next move, where it will explain רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'אך בכור שור או בכור כשב או בכור עז' that the firstborn must be the same kind as its mother. But we just showed that every animal in that verse is needed for the altar law. So where does he find room for his extra rule?
steps.confusionAlert: These two words are a full question. The גמרא often asks 'and what about רבי X?', meaning: how does his view fit with what we just said?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili? (How does he learn his rule?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 40 to challenge רבי יוסי הגלילי's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's use of the verse to teach that a בכור must resemble its mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every animal in the verse is needed for the altar law, nothing is left over for his rule.

steps.title: The word 'בכור' is repeated for no reason
steps.stepSummary: The verse could have said 'firstborn of an ox, lamb, and goat' once. Writing 'בכור' each time is extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have written: 'But the firstborn of an ox, lamb, and goat.' Why do I need 'firstborn', 'firstborn' again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי הגלילי. The animals are needed, but the repeated word 'בכור' is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The altar law only needs the three animal names. The verse instead says 'בכור' before each animal. That extra wording is free for רבי יוסי הגלילי to learn from.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
"But a firstborn ox, lamb, or goat";
why do I need "firstborn" and "firstborn" again?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording (ייתור לשון) frees up a separate teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole verse is used up by the altar law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the animal names are needed for the altar law. The repeated 'בכור' is extra.

steps.title: The firstborn must be the same kind as its mother
steps.stepSummary: The extra 'בכור' teaches that it is a בכור only if the mother is an ox and the baby is an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the law applies only when the mother is an ox and her firstborn is an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what the extra word teaches according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linking 'בכור' to each animal means each firstborn must be of that animal's kind. A cow that gives birth to a baby that looks like a different animal does not create a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, isn't it so? Learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the repeated word 'בכור' that a firstborn must look like its mother.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it correct to learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר.
phrases.english: only when it (the mother) is an ox and its firstborn is an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the rule from the extra word found in step 42.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a בכור must be the same species as its mother.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי הגלילי do with 'פטר חמור' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the משנה learns the 'like its mother' rule from the repeated 'פטר חמור'. What does רבי יוסי הגלילי use it for?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי: what does he do with 'firstborn of a donkey', 'firstborn of a donkey'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the double phrase 'פטר חמור', since he gets the 'like its mother' rule from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'פטר חמור' appears twice in the תורה. The משנה's opinion uses that repetition for the 'like its mother' rule. Since רבי יוסי הגלילי already has another source, those words need a different purpose for him.

keyTerms.meaning: what does he do with it (learn from it)?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
this "firstborn of a donkey", "firstborn of a donkey",
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הַאי ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יוסי הגלילי has his own source, the גמרא asks what he does with the משנה's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the repeated phrase 'פטר חמור'

steps.title: He needs it for a ברייתא about other non-kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: He uses it for a ברייתא. A verse says to redeem the firstborn of non-kosher animals, which might seem to include horses and camels.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: since the verse says, 'But you shall redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem,' I might think even firstborn horses and camels must be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא sets up a possible mistake that the next step will correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in במדבר speaks generally of 'בהמה טמאה' (non-kosher animals). Taken alone, that would include every non-kosher animal, such as horses and camels.

keyTerms.meaning: for that which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught (in a ברייתא):
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
Since it is stated:
"But you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man,
and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem" (במדבר יח:טו),

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ פִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים?
phrases.english: I might understand: even firstborn horses and camels?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses 'פטר חמור' for a ברייתא that limits the redemption law. This step presents the ברייתא's starting worry.

steps.title: Only a donkey, not horses or camels
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'פטר חמור' to teach that only a firstborn donkey needs redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'firstborn of a donkey'. I told you a firstborn donkey, and not firstborn horses and camels.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the answer. The words 'פטר חמור' narrow the law to donkeys only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general phrase 'בהמה טמאה' is narrowed by the specific phrase 'פטר חמור'. So for רבי יוסי הגלילי, the repeated 'פטר חמור' is not wasted. It limits redemption to donkeys.
steps.whatToRemember: Only a firstborn donkey needs redemption, not other non-kosher animals. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns this from 'פטר חמור', while he learns the 'like its mother' rule from the repeated 'בכור'.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that only donkeys need redemption. The question is only which verse each opinion uses for which rule.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "firstborn of a donkey" —
a firstborn donkey I told you,
and not firstborn horses and camels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the possible mistake raised in step 45 and completes the answer to step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, 'פטר חמור' limits the redemption law to donkeys and excludes horses and camels.

steps.title: Maybe horses and camels are still redeemed, just with anything
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא challenges its own derivation. Perhaps 'פטר חמור' does not exclude horses and camels from redemption. Perhaps it only teaches that a donkey is redeemed with a שה, while horses and camels are redeemed with any item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still I can say: firstborn donkeys are redeemed with a lamb, and firstborn horses and camels are redeemed with any item.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא raises a challenge to what it just said. It suggests a different way to read the words 'פטר חמור'. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the בריתא read 'פטר חמור' as limiting the whole מצוה of redemption to donkeys. The challenge says the words may only limit HOW the animal is redeemed, meaning the lamb requirement is for donkeys only. Under this reading, horses and camels would still need redemption, using any object of value.

keyTerms.meaning: "And still I can say": a formula the בריתא uses to raise a remaining possibility against its own derivation
A lamb or kid, the item used to redeem a firstborn donkey
Horses and camels, which are non-kosher animals other than the donkey
With any item, meaning anything of value and not specifically a lamb

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בריתא has now concluded that horses and camels are redeemed. 'ועדיין אני אומר' only raises a possibility that still needs to be answered. The בריתא's real view is still that only donkeys are redeemed.

phrases.english: And still I can say:
firstborn donkeys are redeemed with a lamb,
firstborn horses and camels are redeemed with any item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 46 that 'פטר חמור' limits all redemption to donkeys.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation in Step 46 that only a firstborn donkey needs redemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'פטר חמור' could limit only the lamb requirement to donkeys. In that case horses and camels would not be excluded from redemption altogether, and would be redeemed with any item.
